title: fix(split): preserve native mode when cloning pre-tokenizers
body:
## Problem

Cloning a Split created for a native pre-tokenizer composition reconstructs it through Split::new. For DeepSeek's native composition, the component regexes are intentionally accepted without a general regex backend. A clone therefore panics in a build without fancy-regex. When fancy-regex is enabled, cloning an explicitly native Split instead silently switches its search implementation.

## Change

Reconstruct Search::Unavailable through Split::native. Literal and compiled-regex splits retain their existing construction path.

## Validation

Native Rust tests ran on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu against commit 41c63e663873e0735beef74899520375a1886bb8 in [this workflow](https://github.com/Afloat16/tokenizers/actions/runs/43286040092):

- Without fancy-regex: the new tests fail 3 / pass 2 on unchanged upstream, then all 5 pass with the patch. The existing Split test also passes.
- With fancy-regex: the new tests fail 2 / pass 4 on upstream, then all 6 pass. The 3 existing Split tests pass.
- Tests include loading canonical DeepSeek JSON, cloning its actual pre-tokenizer, and constructing a usable PipelineTokenizer, plus Unicode literal, native-error, and compiled-regex controls.
- Rustfmt passes for the changed files.
- Strict Clippy is blocked in both upstream and patched builds by the same existing needless_range_loop diagnostic in word_cache.rs. The workflow checks that the diagnostic lists match; this is not a claim that strict Clippy passes.

The validation workflow lives on a separate fork branch and is not part of this PR.
